stories.title: Passenger Management & Cabin Selection

coverage.coverageSummary: Covers core passenger count rules (min 1 adult, infant-to-adult constraint, max 9 occupied seats), dynamic passenger summary update, and cabin selection rules (default Economy, single-select cabin). Also covers search gating behavior when invalid passenger composition exists (Search opens the relevant component and does not navigate to SRP).
coverage.coverageReason: Most acceptance criteria and domain passenger rules are covered with positive/negative/boundary scenarios. Coverage is reduced because the requirement does not explicitly define UI behavior for reaching Adult=0 state (UI prevents it) and does not specify exact validation messages, so message-level assertions are avoided.
coveredAreas: Default cabin selection is Economy
Cabin is single-select among Economy/Business/First
Adult minimum enforced (cannot reduce below 1 via UI)
Passenger summary updates dynamically when counts change
Infant count cannot exceed Adult count (including Infant and Infant with Seat)
Max occupied seats = 9, with occupied seats defined as Adults + Children + Infants with Seat
Search does not proceed (no SRP navigation) when passenger rules are violated; missing/invalid component opens
missingAreas: Exact validation messages/content for passenger rule violations (not specified)
Definitive ability to set Adult count to 0 (UI likely prevents; requirement lists as a condition but domain rules state min 1 and minus disabled at 1)
Behavior when total passengers exceeds 9 due to non-seat infants (Infant without seat not counted toward occupied seats; overall max total passenger cap beyond seats not specified)

automationReadiness.reason: Most actions are standard widget interactions (increment/decrement, radio selection, Search click) and can be verified via visible counts and selected cabin. Negative validations rely on absence of SRP navigation and/or popup remaining/opening, which is automatable. Readiness reduced due to potential variability in exact validation presentation (message text not specified) and environment dependence of reaching date selection/SRP without controlled flight/date data.

testCases.title: Verify Economy is selected by default when Guests & Cabin opens
testCases.objective: Confirm default cabin selection is Economy when configuring passengers/cabin.
testCases.confidenceReason: Domain context explicitly states Economy is default and cabin options are radio buttons; validation is observable in the Guests & Cabin popup.
steps: Enter Abu Dhabi in Origin field
Select Abu Dhabi from airport suggestions
Verify selected option Economy cabin radio button is selected
testCases.expectedOutcome: When the Guests & Cabin popup opens after selecting a destination, Economy cabin is selected by default.
testCases.automationReason: Default selected radio button state can be asserted and the journey to open Guests & Cabin is standard UI interaction.

testCases.title: Verify cabin selection is single-select (Business selection deselects Economy)
testCases.objective: Ensure only one cabin class can be selected at a time.
testCases.confidenceReason: Single-select cabin rule is explicit; verification depends on stable radio button selected state.
steps: Enter Abu Dhabi in Origin field
Select Abu Dhabi from airport suggestions
Verify selected option Business cabin radio button is selected
Verify selected option Economy cabin radio button is not selected
testCases.expectedOutcome: Selecting Business results in Business being the only selected cabin class and Economy becoming unselected.
testCases.automationReason: Cabin selection uses radio buttons; selected state can be asserted reliably.

testCases.title: Verify cabin selection is single-select (First selection deselects Business)
testCases.objective: Confirm the single-select behavior holds across multiple cabin switches.
testCases.confidenceReason: Rule is clear; derived scenario increases switching coverage without needing extra business rules.
steps: Enter Abu Dhabi in Origin field
Select Abu Dhabi from airport suggestions
Verify selected option Business cabin radio button is selected
Verify selected option First cabin radio button is selected
Verify selected option Business cabin radio button is not selected
testCases.expectedOutcome: After switching from Business to First, First remains the only selected cabin class.
testCases.automationReason: Sequential radio selection and selected-state assertions are straightforward for Playwright.

testCases.title: Verify Adult minimum of 1 is enforced (Decrease Adult disabled at 1)
testCases.objective: Validate minimum one Adult passenger rule via UI control state.
testCases.confidenceReason: Domain context explicitly states Adult minimum is 1 and minus remains disabled at 1; this is directly verifiable.
steps: Enter Abu Dhabi in Origin field
Select Abu Dhabi from airport suggestions
Verify value Adult passenger count equals 1
Verify selected option Decrease adults control is disabled
testCases.expectedOutcome: The booking widget prevents reducing Adult passengers below 1 by disabling the decrease control when Adult count is 1.
testCases.automationReason: Adult count value and disabled state of decrease control can be asserted.

testCases.title: Verify passenger summary updates dynamically when increasing Adults and Children
testCases.objective: Confirm passenger counts and summary reflect changes immediately.
testCases.confidenceReason: Requirement states dynamic summary update but does not specify exact summary text; validation will focus on count values shown in the Guests & Cabin component.
steps: Enter Abu Dhabi in Origin field
Select Abu Dhabi from airport suggestions
Verify value Adult passenger count equals 2
Verify value Child passenger count equals 1
testCases.expectedOutcome: After adjusting passengers, the displayed passenger counts update immediately to reflect the new values (e.g., Adults=2, Children=1).
testCases.automationReason: Increment actions and visible count assertions are automatable without relying on unspecified message text.

testCases.title: Verify Infant count cannot exceed Adult count (prevent adding second Infant when 1 Adult)
testCases.objective: Ensure the UI prevents an invalid composition where infants exceed adults.
testCases.confidenceReason: Business rule is explicit; however, the exact prevention mechanism (disable vs inline validation) is not specified, so assertions are limited to observable control state/value not exceeding the limit.
steps: Enter Abu Dhabi in Origin field
Select Abu Dhabi from airport suggestions
Verify value Infant passenger count equals 1
Verify selected option Increase infants control is disabled
testCases.expectedOutcome: With 1 Adult selected, the customer cannot increase Infant count beyond 1; the UI blocks the second infant (e.g., by disabling the increase control) and the infant count remains 1.
testCases.automationReason: Count value and control disabled state can be asserted to prove the rule without needing exact message text.

testCases.title: Verify Infant with Seat contributes to occupied seats and seat limit blocks going beyond 9
testCases.objective: Validate the 9 occupied-seat maximum using Adults and Infants with Seat as seat-occupying categories.
testCases.confidenceReason: Seat limit rule is clear, but the UI mechanism for enforcing the limit (disable controls vs message) and whether the widget shows a computed 'seats' summary is not specified; validation focuses on not allowing counts to exceed the boundary.
steps: Enter Abu Dhabi in Origin field
Select Abu Dhabi from airport suggestions
Verify value Adult passenger count equals 9
Verify selected option Increase adults control is disabled
testCases.expectedOutcome: The customer cannot exceed 9 occupied seats in the booking; once the occupied-seat limit is reached, the UI prevents adding additional seat-occupying passengers (e.g., disables further increases).
testCases.automationReason: Repeated increment actions and final count/disabled-state assertions are automatable; does not depend on SRP availability.

testCases.title: Verify occupied seat maximum 9 allows mix of Adults and Children up to 9
testCases.objective: Confirm mixed seat-occupying categories can reach the limit without exceeding it.
testCases.confidenceReason: Underlying rule is clear; UI enforcement specifics are not stated, so assertions focus on final counts reaching the boundary.
steps: Enter Abu Dhabi in Origin field
Select Abu Dhabi from airport suggestions
Verify value Adult passenger count equals 4
Verify value Child passenger count equals 5
testCases.expectedOutcome: The booking widget allows a valid passenger mix where occupied seats equal 9 (e.g., 4 Adults + 5 Children) without blocking the selection.
testCases.automationReason: Count changes and displayed values can be asserted; does not require fare/SRP validation.

testCases.title: Verify Search does not proceed when required passenger rule is violated (infants exceed adults) and prompts completion in relevant component
testCases.objective: Validate that invalid passenger composition prevents search execution and the widget guides the user (no SRP navigation).
testCases.confidenceReason: Requirement states search must not proceed for invalid rules, and domain states Search stays enabled and opens relevant incomplete component; however, reaching an invalid state may be prevented earlier by disabled controls, limiting the ability to test search-blocking at the Search click level.
steps: Enter Abu Dhabi in Origin field
Select Abu Dhabi from airport suggestions
Verify value Infant passenger count equals 1
Verify selected option Increase infants control is disabled
Verify page navigation is not Search Results Page
testCases.expectedOutcome: If passenger rules are not satisfied (or cannot be made invalid due to enforcement), clicking Search must not navigate to the Search Results Page until valid passenger input is provided; the customer remains in the booking flow.
testCases.automationReason: Navigation assertion is automatable, but validating the exact reason (infants exceed adults) at Search time is limited if UI prevents creating the invalid state; also SRP navigation depends on date completeness which is outside this story.

clarifications.question: When a passenger rule is violated (infants exceed adults, or occupied seats > 9), how is the customer informed: disabled +/- controls only, an inline validation message inside Guests & Cabin, or another blocking UI?
clarifications.businessImpact: Determines the correct UAT assertions for negative scenarios (message vs disabled state) and whether we can validate rule enforcement at Search time.

clarifications.question: The acceptance criteria states 'Search must not proceed if Adult count is zero', but domain rules/UI behavior typically prevent Adult from being reduced below 1. Should we treat this as a backend safeguard only (no UI path to Adult=0), or is there a supported user action that can set Adults to 0 (e.g., removing all passengers)?
clarifications.businessImpact: Changes whether a true negative test for Adult=0 can be executed via UI and automated, or whether coverage should rely solely on the minimum-adult UI enforcement.

stories.coverageSummary: Covers core passenger count rules (min 1 adult, infant-to-adult constraint, max 9 occupied seats), dynamic passenger summary update, and cabin selection rules (default Economy, single-select cabin). Also covers search gating behavior when invalid passenger composition exists (Search opens the relevant component and does not navigate to SRP).
stories.description:
DescriptionAs a customer,
I want to configure passengers and cabin preferences,
so that pricing and availability can be calculated correctly.
DetailsPassenger categories shall include:
Adult (12+ Years)

Child (2-11 Years)

Infant (Below 2 Years)

Infant With Seat (Below 2 Years)

Customer shall be able to increase or decrease passenger counts.

Passenger summary shall update dynamically.

Customer shall be able to select:
Economy

Business

First

Additional RequirementsEconomy shall be selected by default.

Only one cabin class can be selected at a time.

Passenger validations shall be evaluated before search execution.

User StoryAs a customer, when booking flights, I want to configure passengers and cabin preferences so that search results accurately reflect my travel requirements.
ContextPassenger configuration directly impacts fare calculation, availability, taxes, and airline operational rules.
Acceptance CriteriaMinimum one Adult passenger must be present.

Maximum occupied seats allowed per booking shall be 9.

Occupied seats shall include:
Adults

Children

Infants With Seat

Infant count must not exceed Adult count.

One Adult can accompany only one Infant.

Search must not proceed if:
Adult count is zero.

Infant count exceeds Adult count.

Total occupied seats exceed nine.

Customer must be able to select Economy, Business, or First cabin.

Economy must be selected by default.

stories.title: Flight Search & Journey Planning

coverage.coverageSummary: Covers core flight-search widget journeys (Round Trip default, One Way, Multi City), mandatory Origin/Destination handling via Search behavior, airport search by code/name/city including popular destinations, key routing validations (same airport, same city, same country), and value retention/clearing behavior when Origin changes. Responsiveness and accessibility are partially covered via basic keyboard validation but full WCAG and device coverage remain gaps.
coverage.coverageReason: Acceptance criteria are mostly covered for journey types, airport search modes, popular destinations, mandatory fields through guided Search behavior, and routing constraints from domain context. Remaining gaps are Open-Jaw (mentioned in description but not supported by domain context/AC), country-configurable nearby airport behavior (requires country-specific data/config), full responsive testing across devices, and comprehensive accessibility standards validation.
coveredAreas: Round Trip is selected by default on widget load
Journey type switching supports One Way and Multi City (and only one selection at a time)
Origin selection using airport code
Origin selection using airport name
Destination selection using city name and selecting an available airport from suggestions
Airport suggestions load dynamically while typing
Popular destinations display when Destination is opened with no typed criteria
Mandatory Origin/Destination enforced through Search opening the incomplete component and preventing SRP navigation
Origin and Destination cannot be identical
Origin and Destination cannot be in the same city (domain rule)
Domestic routing (same country for both airports) not supported (domain rule)
If Origin changes after Destination selection, Destination is cleared and must be reselected
Selected values retained until user modifies them
Guests & Cabin becomes available only after both Origin and Destination are selected; auto-opens after Destination selection
missingAreas: Open-Jaw journey type support (mentioned in story description but not in acceptance criteria/domain supported journey types)
Nearby airport recommendations configurability by country (requires explicit country/config-based expected behavior and test data)
Only active airports selectable (backend-driven; no inactive-airport test data provided to validate exclusion/handling deterministically)
Responsive coverage across desktop/tablet/mobile viewports (requires defined breakpoints/devices to validate)
Accessibility standards coverage beyond basic keyboard navigation (no explicit a11y requirements/criteria supplied)
Promo Code (optional) behavior and validation (listed in widget contents but no business rules/AC provided)

automationReadiness.reason: Most scenarios are UI-driven and deterministically automatable (journey type toggles, suggestions, selection rules, clearing behavior, guided Search). Some requirements depend on environment configuration (nearby airports by country), backend data (active airports), calendar rendering/localization, and broad responsiveness/a11y standards, reducing full automation readiness.

testCases.title: Verify Round Trip is selected by default on Flight Search widget
testCases.objective: Confirm the default journey type on widget load is Round Trip.
testCases.confidenceReason: Domain context explicitly states Round Trip is selected by default when the widget loads; verification is straightforward via selected state.
steps: Verify selected option Round Trip trip type is selected
testCases.expectedOutcome: The flight search widget loads with Round Trip selected as the default journey type.
testCases.automationReason: Selected state of the journey type can be asserted via UI attributes/roles.

testCases.title: Verify airport suggestions load dynamically when typing in Origin using airport code
testCases.objective: Validate dynamic airport suggestions appear while typing an airport code for Origin and can be selected.
testCases.confidenceReason: Requirement states suggestions load dynamically and supports airport code; exact suggestion text is environment-dependent, so validation focuses on suggestion presence and field value update.
steps: Enter Abu Dhabi in Origin field
Select suggestion matching Abu Dhabi from airport suggestions
Verify Origin field value matches the selected airport
testCases.expectedOutcome: Airport suggestions load dynamically while typing an airport code, and selecting a suggestion sets the Origin to the selected airport.
testCases.automationReason: Suggestion content can vary; selecting a specific suggestion reliably may require stable suggestion matching/labels in the environment.

testCases.title: Verify airport suggestions load dynamically when typing in Destination using airport name
testCases.objective: Validate dynamic airport suggestions appear while typing an airport name for Destination and can be selected.
testCases.confidenceReason: Airport-name support is stated, but exact available airport naming in suggestions is not provided; validation focuses on dynamic suggestions and successful selection.
steps: Enter Abu Dhabi in Origin field
Select suggestion matching Abu Dhabi from airport suggestions
Verify Origin field value matches the selected airport
testCases.expectedOutcome: Airport suggestions load dynamically while typing an airport name, and selecting a suggestion sets the Destination to the selected airport.
testCases.automationReason: Suggestion labels may include airport name + code + country; deterministic selection needs stable matching rules.

testCases.title: Verify popular destinations are shown when Destination is opened with no typed criteria
testCases.objective: Validate that popular destinations appear immediately when the Destination field is opened without entering search text.
testCases.confidenceReason: Domain context and requirement both state popular destinations display when Destination is opened with no criteria; can be verified by presence of a popular-destinations section/list.
steps: Verify message Popular destinations are displayed
testCases.expectedOutcome: When the customer opens the Destination field without typing, popular destinations are displayed for selection.
testCases.automationReason: Presence/visibility of the popular destinations container/list can be asserted.

testCases.title: Verify Search guides customer to complete mandatory fields when Origin is missing
testCases.objective: Ensure Origin is enforced as mandatory by preventing search execution and opening the relevant component when missing.
testCases.confidenceReason: AC states Origin mandatory; domain context states Search remains enabled and opens the relevant incomplete component. Exact UI message is unspecified, so validation relies on component opening and lack of navigation to SRP.
steps: Verify Origin selection component is opened
testCases.expectedOutcome: When Search is clicked without a valid Origin, the search is not executed and the Origin selection component opens to guide the customer to complete it.
testCases.automationReason: Depends on reliably detecting the opened Origin component and confirming no SRP navigation without a stable SRP identifier in requirements.

testCases.title: Verify Search guides customer to complete mandatory fields when Destination is missing
testCases.objective: Ensure Destination is enforced as mandatory by preventing search execution and opening the relevant component when missing.
testCases.confidenceReason: AC states Destination mandatory; domain context describes guided behavior. Origin may be pre-populated by geolocation, so the test does not assume Origin is empty; it focuses on missing Destination behavior.
steps: Select suggestion matching AUH from airport suggestions
Verify Destination selection component is opened
testCases.expectedOutcome: When Search is clicked without a valid Destination, the search is not executed and the Destination selection component opens to guide the customer to complete it.
testCases.automationReason: Requires stable detection of the Destination component opening and confirmation that SRP navigation did not occur.

testCases.title: Prevent selecting identical Origin and Destination airports
testCases.objective: Validate the system prevents selecting the same airport for Origin and Destination.
testCases.confidenceReason: Rule is explicit, but the exact validation message and how the UI blocks it (disabling suggestion vs showing message) is not specified; test validates observable prevention via message.
steps: Select suggestion matching AUH from airport suggestions
Select suggestion matching AUH from airport suggestions
Verify message Origin and Destination must be different is displayed
testCases.expectedOutcome: The customer is prevented from setting Destination to the same airport as Origin; a validation is shown and the invalid route is not accepted.
testCases.automationReason: Exact validation text is not provided; automation may need to assert a generic error container/state rather than a fixed message.

testCases.title: Prevent selecting Origin and Destination in the same city
testCases.objective: Validate the system prevents selecting two different airports that belong to the same city.
testCases.confidenceReason: Domain context defines the rule, but no concrete city with multiple airports is provided to select deterministically in this environment.
steps: Select suggestion matching CityWithMultipleAirports from airport suggestions
Verify same-city airports are excluded from Destination suggestions
testCases.expectedOutcome: The customer is prevented from creating a route where Origin and Destination are in the same city, even if they are different airports.
testCases.automationReason: Requires environment-specific data where a city returns multiple bookable airports and the UI exposes them clearly; without known selectable suggestions, automation cannot be deterministic.

testCases.title: Prevent domestic routing when both airports are in the same country
testCases.objective: Validate the system blocks routes where Origin and Destination are in the same country.
testCases.confidenceReason: Domain context states domestic routes are not supported, but no specific same-country airport pairs are provided; behavior/message is not specified.
steps: Select suggestion matching OriginSameCountry from airport suggestions
Verify message Domestic routing is not supported is displayed
testCases.expectedOutcome: The customer is prevented from searching a domestic route where both selected airports are in the same country.
testCases.automationReason: Requires curated airport pairs known to be in the same country and selectable in the environment; without defined test data, automation is not deterministic.

testCases.title: Verify changing Origin after selecting Destination clears Destination
testCases.objective: Confirm destination is automatically cleared when origin is changed after destination selection.
testCases.confidenceReason: Domain context explicitly defines this behavior; can be verified by observing Destination field becomes empty/cleared.
steps: Select suggestion matching AUH from airport suggestions
Select suggestion matching BOM from airport suggestions
Select suggestion matching DEL from airport suggestions
Verify Destination is cleared after changing Origin
testCases.expectedOutcome: After the customer changes the Origin when a Destination was already selected, the system automatically clears the Destination and requires the customer to select Destination again.
testCases.automationReason: Cleared-state assertion depends on how the field represents empty (blank text vs placeholder); needs stable way to assert empty value.

testCases.title: Verify One Way journey type can be selected and remains the only selected trip type
testCases.objective: Validate One Way is selectable and mutually exclusive with Round Trip.
testCases.confidenceReason: Journey type support and mutual exclusivity are clear in domain context; selection state can be asserted.
steps: Verify selected option One Way trip type is selected
Verify selected option Round Trip trip type is not selected
testCases.expectedOutcome: The customer can switch to One Way, and only One Way remains selected (Round Trip is deselected).
testCases.automationReason: Trip type controls and selected states are verifiable via UI attributes.

testCases.title: Verify Multi City journey type can be selected and Flight 1 Destination receives focus
testCases.objective: Validate Multi City can be selected and initial focus behavior follows the defined flow.
testCases.confidenceReason: Domain context defines Multi City focus behavior; however focus assertions can be brittle depending on implementation and accessibility tree.
steps: Verify page navigation Multi City itinerary inputs are displayed
Verify selected option Multi City trip type is selected
testCases.expectedOutcome: The customer can select Multi City and the widget displays the multi-segment itinerary inputs with Multi City selected.
testCases.automationReason: Multi City selection and presence of segment inputs can be asserted; avoids fragile focus-specific assertion.

testCases.title: Verify Guests & Cabin cannot be accessed before selecting both Origin and Destination
testCases.objective: Ensure Guests & Cabin is blocked until both Origin and Destination are selected.
testCases.confidenceReason: Domain context explicitly states Guests & Cabin cannot be accessed until both Origin and Destination are selected; behavior can be asserted via blocked interaction or message.
testCases.expectedOutcome: The customer cannot open Guests & Cabin selection until both Origin and Destination have been selected.
testCases.automationReason: UI may block by disabling control or showing no response; automation must detect disabled state or a consistent blocking message.

testCases.title: Verify selected Origin and Destination values are retained until modified
testCases.objective: Confirm the widget retains selected airport values while the user interacts with other components.
testCases.confidenceReason: Retention rule is explicit; can be validated by selecting values then interacting with journey type or opening/closing components and rechecking values.
steps: Select suggestion matching AUH from airport suggestions
Select suggestion matching BOM from airport suggestions
Verify Origin and Destination values are retained
testCases.expectedOutcome: After selecting Origin and Destination, the widget retains the selected values until the customer explicitly changes them.
testCases.automationReason: Retention across journey-type changes may vary (some implementations reset fields); if reset is intended, requirement would conflict—needs stable expected behavior confirmation.

testCases.title: Verify basic keyboard accessibility for selecting a Destination from popular destinations
testCases.objective: Validate a minimal accessibility behavior: user can reach Destination and select an option without a mouse.
testCases.confidenceReason: Requirement states components should meet accessibility standards, but no explicit criteria are provided; test limits to a basic keyboard-driven interaction.
steps: Select the first popular destination using the keyboard
testCases.expectedOutcome: A customer can select a destination from Popular destinations using accessible interactions, and the Destination field reflects the chosen value.
testCases.automationReason: True keyboard-only validation requires keypress actions and focus assertions; with limited step patterns, this is only partially automatable.

clarifications.question: The story description includes Open-Jaw journey type, but acceptance criteria and domain context list only Round Trip, One Way, and Multi City as supported. Should Open-Jaw be supported in this release for AIT-6?
clarifications.businessImpact: If Open-Jaw is in scope, additional journey-type UI, routing rules, date logic, and SRP expectations require separate UAT and automation coverage; excluding it reduces functional coverage versus the stated customer intent.

clarifications.question: What is the expected observable behavior for 'Nearby airport recommendations configurable by country' (e.g., a labeled 'Nearby airports' section, ordering rules, distance threshold), and which country configurations should be validated in UAT?
clarifications.businessImpact: Without explicit expected behavior and target countries, testing cannot confirm the configurability requirement and may miss misconfiguration impacting conversion for specific markets.

clarifications.question: When a user attempts an invalid route (same airport, same city, or same country), what exact in-component validation outcome is expected (message text or UI state), and should the invalid selection be blocked or allowed but corrected later?
clarifications.businessImpact: Different outcomes change both UAT assertions and automated checks; ambiguity risks false failures or missed validation defects that prevent booking.

clarifications.question: Promo Code is listed as part of the search widget. What are the business rules for promo code entry (format/length, case sensitivity), and what is the expected behavior if an invalid promo code is entered at search time?
clarifications.businessImpact: Without rules, promo code validation and customer guidance cannot be tested; errors here can lead to revenue leakage or customer frustration.

clarifications.question: For responsiveness requirement, which device categories/viewports must be validated for UAT sign-off (specific breakpoints or representative devices for desktop/tablet/mobile)?
clarifications.businessImpact: Without defined targets, responsive testing may be incomplete, potentially missing layout/interaction issues on key devices that block search initiation.

stories.coverageSummary: Covers core flight-search widget journeys (Round Trip default, One Way, Multi City), mandatory Origin/Destination handling via Search behavior, airport search by code/name/city including popular destinations, key routing validations (same airport, same city, same country), and value retention/clearing behavior when Origin changes. Responsiveness and accessibility are partially covered via basic keyboard validation but full WCAG and device coverage remain gaps.
stories.description:
DescriptionAs a customer,
I want to search for flights using Round Trip, One-Way, Multi-City, and Open-Jaw journey types,
so that I can discover available flights based on my travel requirements and proceed with booking.
DetailsFlight Search widget shall be available on the homepage and booking landing pages.

Customer shall be able to search flights using:
Round Trip

One Way

Multi-City

Round Trip shall be selected by default.

Search widget shall contain:
Origin

Destination

Travel Date(s)

Guests & Cabin

Promo Code (Optional)

Search Button

Airport search shall support:
Airport Code

Airport Name

City Name

System shall display:
Airport suggestions

Popular destinations

Nearby airports

Nearby airport recommendations shall be configurable by country.

Origin and Destination airports must be different.

Only active airports shall be available for booking.

Search widget shall support desktop, tablet, and mobile devices.

Additional RequirementsAirport suggestions shall load dynamically while typing.

Popular destinations shall be displayed when no search criteria is entered.

Nearby airport recommendations shall be configurable through CMS/business configuration.

Search widget shall retain selected values until user modifies them.

Search components shall meet accessibility standards.

User StoriesStory 1As a customer, when I start planning a trip, I want to search and select departure and destination airports so that I can define my travel route.
Story 2As a customer, when searching for flights, I want airport suggestions and nearby airport recommendations so that I can easily find suitable travel options.
ContextFlight Search is the primary entry point of the booking journey. Customers must be able to search flights across supported journey types while adhering to airline routing and airport validation rules.
Acceptance CriteriaFlight Search widget must support Round Trip, One-Way, and Multi-City journeys.

Round Trip must be selected by default.

Origin airport must be mandatory.

Destination airport must be mandatory.

Origin and Destination airports must not be identical.

Airport search must support Airport Code, Airport Name, and City Name.

Popular destinations must be displayed when applicable.

Nearby airport suggestions must be configurable by country.

Only active airports must be selectable.

Search widget must be responsive across supported devices.

stories.title: Promo Code, Loyalty Booking & Fare Configuration

coverage.coverageSummary: Covers promo code entry availability, validation on Search, invalid promo code messaging, loyalty search mode, and loyalty calendar behavior (no revenue fare amounts while still showing availability indicators). Includes derived risk scenarios for missing required fields and mode switching to ensure promo code validation is still enforced during search execution.
coverage.coverageReason: Acceptance criteria are largely covered, but pricing-impact verification for valid promo codes cannot be fully asserted without controlled pricing expectations, and specific error message text for invalid promo codes is unspecified. Calendar 'availability visible' is covered at an indicator level (presence of selectable/available dates without fare amounts), but exact availability representation is not defined.
coveredAreas: Promo code field is present and accepts input
Promo code validation occurs during Search execution (not inline)
Invalid promo code triggers a validation message during search flow
Search flow guidance when required inputs missing still works with promo code present
Loyalty redemption search mode can be enabled and searched
Loyalty calendar does not show revenue fare amounts
Loyalty availability remains visible in calendar experience
missingAreas: Defined, testable expected pricing change for a known valid promo code (baseline vs discounted) and where it is observed (SRP price, summary, fare breakdown)
Authoritative invalid promo code validation message text(s) and where displayed (promo code component vs modal/toast)
Whether promo codes are allowed/ignored/blocked in loyalty redemption mode
How loyalty availability is represented in calendar (e.g., 'Available' label, dots, selectable dates) for deterministic verification

automationReadiness.reason: Most actions are standard UI interactions and validations (field presence, messages, navigation) and are suitable for Playwright. However, deterministic validation of 'valid promo codes must impact search pricing' requires stable test data and a predictable pricing assertion, and loyalty calendar rendering/availability indicators may vary by locale/session.

testCases.title: Verify Promo code field is available and accepts input
testCases.objective: Confirm the customer can access a Promo code field and enter a promotional code value for flight search.
testCases.confidenceReason: Requirement explicitly states promo code field must be available; validating field presence and text entry is deterministic.
steps: Enter PROMO10 in Promo code field
Verify Promo code field value equals PROMO10
testCases.expectedOutcome: A Promo code field is available on the flight search experience and allows the customer to enter and retain a promo code value.
testCases.automationReason: Field presence, text entry, and value verification are directly automatable with Playwright.

testCases.title: Invalid promo code is validated during Search and shows a validation message
testCases.objective: Ensure an invalid promo code is not accepted and produces a validation message during Search execution (not requiring inline validation).
testCases.confidenceReason: Validation timing is clear (during Search), but exact error message content/location is not defined, reducing assertion specificity.
steps: Enter Abu Dhabi in Origin field
Select Abu Dhabi from airport suggestions
Enter INVALIDCODE in Promo code field
Verify message indicates promo code is invalid
testCases.expectedOutcome: When Search is executed with an invalid promo code, the system blocks successful search execution and displays a validation message indicating the promo code is invalid.
testCases.automationReason: Search flow and message presence are automatable, but without specified message text or a stable message container, assertion may need more resilient matching.

testCases.title: Promo code validation occurs on Search execution (no immediate blocking before Search)
testCases.objective: Confirm promo code is validated as part of Search execution rather than requiring immediate inline validation on field entry.
testCases.confidenceReason: Requirement states validation occurs during search; however, it does not explicitly state that inline validation never occurs, so expectation is limited to not requiring it.
steps: Enter INVALIDCODE in Promo code field
Verify message is not displayed for promo code
testCases.expectedOutcome: Entering a promo code does not require immediate validation feedback; validation is performed during Search execution (a validation message, if any, is not required to appear at entry time).
testCases.automationReason: Absence-of-message checks can be flaky without defined UI behavior; requires clear identification of where such message would appear.

testCases.title: Valid promo code impacts search pricing (pricing model change observed)
testCases.objective: Validate that a known valid promo code affects pricing when searching for flights.
testCases.confidenceReason: Requirement states pricing impact, but there is no defined valid promo code, no baseline price, and no guaranteed availability; observable pricing change cannot be deterministically asserted without controlled test data.
steps: Enter Abu Dhabi in Origin field
Select Abu Dhabi from airport suggestions
Enter PROMO10 in Promo code field
Verify page navigation to Search Results Page
testCases.expectedOutcome: Search completes and navigates to the Search Results Page, and the returned pricing reflects the applied valid promo code according to promotional pricing rules.
testCases.automationReason: Navigation to SRP is automatable, but verifying pricing impact requires known expected price deltas or a stable indicator that a promo was applied.

testCases.title: Search with missing required inputs opens relevant component even when promo code is entered
testCases.objective: Ensure the booking widget still guides the user to complete required fields when Search is clicked, regardless of promo code entry.
testCases.confidenceReason: Domain context defines Search opens relevant incomplete component when required fields are missing; promo code should not break this guidance.
steps: Enter PROMO10 in Promo code field
Verify message indicates missing required trip details
testCases.expectedOutcome: When Search is clicked without completing required trip inputs, the application does not execute search and guides the customer to complete missing information, even if a promo code was entered.
testCases.automationReason: The opening of the incomplete component is automatable, but the requirement does not define a specific message; verification may need to rely on a generic guidance indicator.

testCases.title: Enable loyalty redemption search mode and perform a search
testCases.objective: Confirm loyalty redemption (reward flight) search mode is available and supports flight search.
testCases.confidenceReason: Requirement clearly states loyalty mode must be supported, but exact control label and required member authentication are not specified in requirement/domain context.
steps: Verify selected option equals Loyalty redemption
Enter Abu Dhabi in Origin field
Select Abu Dhabi from airport suggestions
Verify page navigation to Search Results Page
testCases.expectedOutcome: Customer can enable loyalty redemption search mode and execute a reward flight search that navigates to the Search Results Page for reward availability.
testCases.automationReason: If loyalty mode is behind authentication or the control label differs, automation needs stable UI identifiers and possibly member setup.

testCases.title: Loyalty calendar does not display revenue fare amounts while still showing availability
testCases.objective: Validate loyalty calendar experience hides cash fare amounts and still indicates availability in a non-revenue form.
testCases.confidenceReason: Requirement specifies 'no fare amounts' and 'availability visible' but does not define what constitutes an availability indicator or the exact calendar UI behavior in all locales.
steps: Verify selected option equals Loyalty redemption
Enter Abu Dhabi in Origin field
Select Abu Dhabi from airport suggestions
Verify page navigation to Date Picker
Verify message shows no fare amounts in calendar
testCases.expectedOutcome: When loyalty redemption search is enabled, the calendar experience does not expose revenue fare amounts (cash prices), while still indicating which dates have reward availability.
testCases.automationReason: Calendar UI assertions are feasible, but require a defined, stable indicator for 'fare amounts not displayed' and 'availability visible' across sessions/locales.

testCases.title: Switch between cash and loyalty modes and ensure the selected pricing model persists to Search
testCases.objective: Mitigate risk of mode confusion by ensuring switching pricing models updates the search mode and persists through Search execution.
testCases.confidenceReason: Requirement mentions separate pricing rules but not explicit persistence behavior; still a common high-risk journey issue that can be validated via selected option and SRP navigation.
steps: Verify selected option equals Loyalty redemption
Verify selected option equals Cash booking
Enter Abu Dhabi in Origin field
Select Abu Dhabi from airport suggestions
Verify page navigation to Search Results Page
testCases.expectedOutcome: Customer can switch between loyalty redemption and cash booking modes, the latest selected mode remains active, and search executes using that selected pricing model.
testCases.automationReason: Mode selection, selected-state verification, and SRP navigation are automatable if the mode controls are accessible.

clarifications.question: What are the exact validation message(s) and display location when a promo code is invalid (e.g., inline under promo field, banner, toast, modal)?
clarifications.businessImpact: Without defined message/location, UAT and automation can only assert a generic 'invalid promo' indication, reducing confidence and increasing false failures.

clarifications.question: Provide at least one known valid promo code for test/UAT and define the observable pricing impact to verify (e.g., percentage discount, waived fee, or an 'Applied promo' indicator on SRP).
clarifications.businessImpact: Cannot deterministically validate the acceptance criterion 'Valid promo codes must impact search pricing' without controlled promo code and expected outcome.

clarifications.question: Are promo codes allowed in loyalty redemption mode, and if not allowed, what is the expected customer behavior (ignored, blocked with message, or disabled field)?
clarifications.businessImpact: Mode interaction affects core journeys and pricing rules; unclear behavior may lead to incorrect customer expectations and missed defects.

clarifications.question: In loyalty calendar experience, how is 'loyalty availability remains visible' represented (e.g., selectable dates, 'Available' label, point amounts, seat count, dots), and what should be asserted in UAT?
clarifications.businessImpact: Without a defined availability indicator, tests cannot reliably validate that availability is visible while revenue fare amounts are hidden.

stories.coverageSummary: Covers promo code entry availability, validation on Search, invalid promo code messaging, loyalty search mode, and loyalty calendar behavior (no revenue fare amounts while still showing availability indicators). Includes derived risk scenarios for missing required fields and mode switching to ensure promo code validation is still enforced during search execution.
stories.description:
DescriptionAs a customer,
I want to apply promotional and loyalty benefits,
so that eligible discounts and rewards can be considered during flight search.
DetailsCustomer shall be able to enter a promo code.

Promo code validation shall occur during search.

Valid promo codes shall be applied to pricing and availability.

Invalid promo codes shall display appropriate error messages.

Loyalty redemption search shall be supported.

Additional RequirementsLoyalty booking mode and fare booking mode shall follow separate pricing rules.

Loyalty calendar experience shall not expose revenue fare information.

User StoriesStory 1As a customer, when I have a promotional code, I want the code validated during flight search so that applicable discounts are applied.
Story 2As a loyalty member, I want to search for reward flights so that I can redeem my loyalty points.
ContextFlight search must support multiple pricing models including cash bookings, promotional fares, and loyalty redemption bookings.
Acceptance CriteriaPromo code field must be available.

Promo code validation must occur during search execution.

Invalid promo codes must display validation messages.

Valid promo codes must impact search pricing.

Loyalty search mode must be supported.

Calendar fare amounts must not be displayed when loyalty search is enabled.

Loyalty availability must remain visible.
